composition: C: the whole facade small at the top seen from across the street, the headline large in the lawn snow, five hanging wooden signs on a post at the foot of the walk, Choose a room section starting below.
prompt: A mobile landing page at phone viewport, portrait, for Wander Niagara, rendered edge to edge as a real web page with crisp readable text, no phone frame, no browser chrome. The visitor is planning a winter day trip or overnight to St. Catharines and the Benchlands and the page is the view from across the street of a house to enter. Parts in reading order: a slim header on the night sky with a small white "Wander" wordmark at left and one small engraved brass plaque button "What's on" at right. The top third of the screen: the whole symmetrical red-brick Georgian colonial at night, five bays wide with two dormers, between two bare oaks, every window glowing amber through sheer curtains with a candle in each, warm-white mini-lights outlining every window and the arched white portico, a wreath with a red bow on the black front door, a lit brass lantern, lit shrubs along the foundation, snow on the roof, slow falling snow. The middle third: the deep snow of the front lawn, blue in shadow and amber where the windows throw light, with the bluestone walk leading up to the door; set large in the snow as type: "Winter is made for wandering", and beneath it the subline "A holiday escape to St. Catharines and the Benchlands." The bottom third: at the foot of the walk, a wooden signpost in the snow with five hanging wooden signs, each pointing up toward the house, lettered "What's on this winter", "Eat, drink and shop", "Winter outdoors", "Stay the night", "Winter reading"; below the signpost a page section starts with a thin brass rule and the heading "Choose a room". Visual law: a warm navy night sky, never black. A heavy, friendly 1990 greeting-card serif in snow white. Brass plaques with engraved lettering. Warm inside, cold outside; film-grain warmth.
